title: Introduction to cori.data.hu
text: Housing stock per capita diverges rural nonrural counties. chart shows population-weighted average housing units per 1,000 population rural status using CBSA 2023 rural definition.
code: library(cori.charts) library(ggplot2) library(ruraldefinitions) library(dplyr)  load_fonts()  df <- get_housing_units(   geography = "county",   variables = "housing_units_per_1k_people" )  rural_avg <- df |>   left_join(select(cbsa_2023, geoid, is_rural), by = "geoid") |>   filter(!is.na(is_rural), !is.na(value), !is.na(agg_var)) |>   group_by(year, is_rural) |>   summarise(     value = sum(value * agg_var, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(agg_var, na.rm = TRUE),     .groups = "drop"   )  ggplot(rural_avg, aes(x = year, y = value, color = is_rural)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   geom_point(size = 2.5) +   scale_color_manual(     values = c("Rural" = "#2F6E9B", "Nonrural" = "#7EBDC2"),     labels = c("Rural" = "Rural counties", "Nonrural" = "Nonrural counties")   ) +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2000, 2024, by = 5)) +   scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1)) +   theme_cori() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom") +   labs(     title    = "Rural counties carry more housing units per capita than nonrural",     subtitle = "Population-weighted average housing units per 1,000 population, 2000\u20132024",     x        = NULL,     y        = NULL,     color    = NULL,     caption  = "Source: CORI analysis of U.S. Census Bureau Housing Unit Estimates."   )

title: Introduction to cori.data.hu
code: grafton <- get_housing_units(   variables = "housing_units_per_1k_people",   geoids    = c("33009", "33", "00") ) |>   mutate(     group = case_when(       geoid == "33009" ~ "Grafton County, NH",       geoid == "33"    ~ "New Hampshire",       geoid == "00"    ~ "United States"     ),     group = factor(group, levels = c("Grafton County, NH", "New Hampshire", "United States"))   )  ggplot(grafton, aes(x = year, y = value, color = group, linetype = group, linewidth = group)) +   geom_line(na.rm = TRUE) +   geom_point(size = 2.5, na.rm = TRUE) +   scale_color_manual(values = c(     "Grafton County, NH" = "#2F6E9B",     "New Hampshire"      = "#7EBDC2",     "United States"      = "#9DA7B0"   )) +   scale_linetype_manual(values = c(     "Grafton County, NH" = "solid",     "New Hampshire"      = "dashed",     "United States"      = "dotted"   )) +   scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(     "Grafton County, NH" = 1.2,     "New Hampshire"      = 0.8,     "United States"      = 0.8   )) +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2000, 2024, by = 5)) +   scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1)) +   theme_cori() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom") +   labs(     title    = "Housing units per 1,000 residents — Grafton County, NH",     subtitle = "Compared to New Hampshire and the United States, 2000\u20132024",     x        = NULL,     y        = NULL,     color    = NULL,     linetype = NULL,     linewidth = NULL,     caption  = paste0(       "Source: CORI analysis of U.S. Census Bureau Housing Unit Estimates.\n",       "Population denominator from Census Population Estimates Program via cori.data.pep."     )   )

title: Access and Analyze Census Bureau Housing Unit Estimates
text: U.S. Census Bureau’s National, State, County Housing Unit Totals (also called Housing Unit Estimates) annual estimates total number housing units existence. Published Population Estimates Program, measure total housing stock — just new construction activity. package measures housing stock — total number units exist point time — opposed construction activity permitting flow. Official source name: National, State, County Housing Unit Totals Producer: U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program Vintage designation: e.g., “Vintage 2024” covers April 1, 2020 – July 1, 2024 Coverage: Annual estimates 2000 present (anchored decennial census) Geography: National, state, county (5-digit FIPS) Release cadence: Annually, typically May Dataset page: https://www.census.gov/data/datasets/time-series/demo/popest/2020s-total-housing-units.html

title: Access and Analyze Census Bureau Housing Unit Estimates
text: structure type breakdown public release — single-family vs. multifamily available level (use BPS distinction) vacancy occupancy status — count total units regardless occupancy; pair ACS vacancy rates Loss rates static — derived 2009/2011 AHS, applied unchanged across vintages Non-permitted construction distributed West — methodology gap Western counties without permit offices County smallest public geography — subcounty (city/town) estimates exist internally Census released Estimates, counts — values modeled; decennial census direct count

what: Caution: Do Not Compute Net Change Across Decade Series
title: Access and Analyze Census Bureau Housing Unit Estimates
text: subtract housing unit values across 2009→2010 2019→2020 boundaries. dataset assembled three independent Census decade series (2000s, 2010s, 2020s), anchored decennial Census baseline. 2010 2020 values fresh Census counts — continuations prior series estimate. Subtracting across boundaries produces arithmetic difference reflects potential methodological inconsistencies, real changes housing stock. example, 2020 Census counted fewer units county 2010s series projected 2019, difference appear housing loss — even demolitions occurred. year--year change analysis: restrict single decade series (e.g., 2020–2024 ) use permit data cori.data.bps proxy net new construction within series.

title: Get Census Bureau housing unit estimates — get_housing_units
text: geography Character. Geographic level return: "", "county", "state", "nation". Ignored geoids provided. Default: "". years Integer vector. Years return. Default: available. geoids Character vector. FIPS codes return (5-digit county, 2-digit state, "00" national). provided, takes precedence geography. Default: NULL (geographies). variables Character vector. Variables return: "housing_units", "housing_units_per_1k_people", /"housing_unit_change". Default: . See get_hu_codebook() details. vintage Character. Vintage read, e.g. "2024". Default: "latest".

title: Get Census Bureau housing unit estimates — get_housing_units

title: Get the housing unit variable codebook — get_hu_codebook
code: get_hu_codebook() #>                      variable                raw_variable #> 1               housing_units               housing_units #> 2 housing_units_per_1k_people housing_units_per_1k_people #> 3         housing_unit_change         housing_unit_change #>                                label                    unit nominal #> 1                Total housing units                   units   FALSE #> 2 Housing units per 1,000 population units per 1,000 persons   FALSE #> 3        Net change in housing units                   units   FALSE #>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         notes #> 1 Annual July 1 estimate of total housing units (occupied + vacant). Built from decennial Census baseline plus permitted construction, non-permitted construction, mobile home shipments, and housing loss. Coverage: 2000-present (2000-2009 intercensal, 2010-2019, 2020-present). Geography: county (5-digit FIPS), state (2-digit FIPS), national ('00'). #> 2                                                                                                                Total housing units divided by population in thousands. Population denominator from Census Population Estimates Program via cori.data.pep. Coverage: 2000-present. agg_var = population / 1,000, suitable for population-weighted averaging. #> 3                            Year-over-year net change in total housing units. NA for 2000, 2010, and 2020 — these boundary years span different decade series with different Census baselines, so the arithmetic difference reflects a methodological reset rather than real housing stock change. Coverage: 2001-present (excluding decade boundary years).
